main_text.head: CAP. XXXIV.
Rationes dissuadentes singulare certamen, proponuntur.
main_text.p: QUia vero non Barbaris aut Ethnicis, verum Christianis potissimum scribo, ideo nonnulla duella dissuadentia in medium proferam; quibus forte animus, non in totum depravatus, sisti possit, ne ruat ad vindictam per grande periculum. Quisquis igitur in duella proclivis est, & facile ad ea provocat, cogitet, sese idque ex illo trito, miserum futurum: quod provocatores raro sint fælices. Aristot. libr.9.de Animal. Ut illis id eveniat saepe, quod de cignis refert Aristoteles. Nunquam pugnam inchoant, impetiti autem ab aquilis semper superiores existunt. Idque juxta illud Antiphontis, oratoris Attici: In-ci-

page.notes: Transcription corrections: the printed text reads "Christianis", "sisti possit" and "ruat" as shown; the note marks "Aristot." and "Animal." are in the left margin. The final line ends with a catchword-like fragment "ci-" which continues onto the next page as "ci-" (hyphenated "inci-"); it is kept as printed. Words "fælices", "Ut", "Antiphontis" and "Attici" were read with confidence; "saepe" was read as printed. The number "294" is at the top left. A faint library stamp at the bottom right ("Google") was excluded.
